subject: CAIQ control stitching plan & artifact index
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Li <dana.li@healthnet.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ control stitching plan & artifact index

Hi Dana —

Following our kickoff call last week, attached is a lightweight proposal for how we plan to stitch CAIQ questions back to our control artifacts so you can consume a single indexed package rather than many siloed files. Key points: 

- We will create an "artifact index" (attached CSV) that maps each CAIQ question to 1..N evidence items (config exports, runbooks, logs, attestations).
- For runtime controls we will include a small pseudonymized log snippet and a short description of why the snippet satisfies the assertion.
- Where a CAIQ control is met by process + technical evidence, both will be referenced and evidence owners assigned.

Attachments: CAIQ_Control_Stitch_Template.xlsx, evidence_index_v0.9.csv

Proposed timeline:
- Today: share template and initial index (attached)
- Tue (05/18): replace placeholders with final artifact links and owner names
- Fri (05/21): deliver zipped CAIQ package for your review

Would you be able to confirm your procurement/compliance contact who needs the final package? I copied Jonas and Kimberly to own the artifact assembly and control verification.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

---
Note: The attached index contains placeholder references to runtime logs (sample file: sample-runtime-log-snippet.txt) — those are redacted examples; full artifacts will be delivered via a secure share once owners confirm access levels.

From: Dana Li <dana.li@healthnet.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ control stitching plan & artifact index

Thanks Marissa — this looks promising and much easier to consume than separate PDFs. Couple of clarifying items: 

1) For controls referencing logging/monitoring, can you include the log retention policy link and a single full-day sample (redacted) rather than just a snippet? Our auditors prefer longer traces for sampling.
2) On keys: we need a KMS attestation and the key rotation policy. If you can point us to the HSM/KMS artifact, that will speed up the review.

Procurement touchpoint is Michael Ortiz (procurement@healthnet.com) — I will loop him in once we have the delivery plan.

Best,
Dana Li
Security Assurance Lead
HealthNet Solutions
dana.li@healthnet.com
+1 (617) 555-2299

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Li <dana.li@healthnet.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ control stitching plan & artifact index

Hi Dana —

Thanks for the quick review and the ask. Yes, we can do both: a full-day redacted log bundle (delivered on secure link) and a detailed KMS/HSM attestation PDF. To make this repeatable, Jonas and I propose the following additions to the index: 

- evidence_type: {config_export, runbook, log_bundle, attestation}
- retention_policy_link: URL per artifact
- access_instructions: short note about how auditors request access (SCP to our S3 share)

Action items: 
- Jonas: produce redacted 24-hour runtime logs for the example control (owner: Jonas Weber)
- Kimberly: gather KMS attestation and key rotation policy (owner: Kimberly Park)
- Marissa: update index with evidence_type and retention_policy fields, and generate the final zip manifest

Can you confirm if HealthNet requires logs with original timestamps preserved or if obfuscated timestamps are acceptable for the initial pass?

Thanks — planning to have the updated index back to you by EOD Tue (05/18).

Regards,
Marissa

Subject: Re: CAIQ control stitching plan & artifact index — log runbook and sample

Marissa / team —

I've attached a short runbook and a sample script I used to extract a 24-hour redacted log bundle for the control in question. Notes: 

- The script strips IPs and user identifiers, preserves event order and timestamps (optionally obfuscated).
- Output format: ndjson, zipped and checksummed.
- I also ran a small verification against our continuous compliance check that flags anomalies — results included as a small CSV in the runbook.

Attachment: stitcher-runbook.md, sample-runtime-log-snippet.txt

Putting Evelyn on the thread to confirm whether we need to pull the logs from the dedicated ingest cluster or the archived cold store for retention purposes.

—Jonas
Engineering Manager, Runtime
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
